title: Truncated VISp-axis powers and full spectra do not identify variance outside the VISp span
abstract: We tested what the saved cross-basis results identify about new stimulus directions in higher mouse visual areas. Two exact response kernels have the same first-30 VISp-axis powers, full target spectrum, and total variance. One is inside a fixed 64-dimensional VISp span. The other has 20 percent of its variance outside that span. A signed linear readout makes the first kernel from a full-support source. Thus the measured preference for new dominant axes does not alone establish new span dimensions. An audit of the published aggregate arrays finds that they save only the first 100 cross-axis powers and omit cross-axis covariance. We derive a four-partition block audit that separates covariance within a chosen span, variance outside it, and coupling between them. Its unnormalized estimates are unbiased under independent zero-mean repeat noise and fixed preprocessing. Independent-noise simulations pass numerical checks; shared-noise controls fail. This is a proof and method result. It does not show that rotation explains the mouse data, recover semantic features, or reject the reported spectral hierarchy. Code, licensed aggregate input, exact kernels, provenance, and offline reproduction steps are included.

display.caption: Two kernels have the same measured axis powers, full spectrum and trace, but different variance outside a fixed full VISp span. A four-partition block audit separates within-span covariance and outside trace in synthetic repeat-noise tests.
